title: The Problem of Induction
text:
Inductive reasoning involves drawing generalized conclusions from a limited set of specific observations. While foundational to scientific methodology, this process faces profound philosophical skepticism regarding its certainty. The core challenge, highlighted by David Hume, is that past successful conjunctions do not logically guarantee future outcomes; the assumption that nature operates consistently across time remains an unproven premise.

This deficiency suggests that knowledge derived solely from empirical observation may be probabilistic rather than absolutely certain. Therefore, fields such as philosophy of science must rigorously analyze what constitutes sufficient justification for universal laws and predictions.
